analysis.root_cause_title: Automatic retry after acknowledgement timeout caused a second execution under the same instruction
analysis.root_cause_explanation: The records show one customer-originated request and then a system-originated retry tied to the same business instruction. Request 1caca9dd-3b63-4482-b290-ffa404164f84 was received first, completed successfully, and posted a verified journal. After an ACK timeout and retry scheduling, request f0385f1f-12b8-4796-9ecc-15c828ed65ae was submitted as an automatic retry referencing the original payment and the same correlation/business instruction, then also completed and posted a verified journal. This supports a shared-instruction duplicate request/execution pattern rather than two independently authorized instructions. The exact physical trigger for the repeat is not evidenced; the records only show the system retry path after timeout.

The first payment was customer-originated, received at 2026-11-11T15:40:40.269373+00:00, and completed with posting.

hypotheses.statement: The duplicate execution was caused by an automatic retry after an acknowledgement timeout rather than a second independent customer instruction.
The repeated submission may have been driven by system retry logic; the physical user action, if any, is not evidenced.

uncertainty: The primary records do not show a human authorization event for the second request; outcome fields are NOT_RECORDED.
The literal trigger for the retry cannot be determined from the available data, and no input-device evidence is present.
A shared instruction is strongly indicated by the retry linkage and common business instruction, but the records do not expose the detector configuration or exact causal rule path.
analysis.recommendation_reason: Two verified posted payments exist under the same business instruction, with the second generated as an automatic retry after timeout. This is a confirmed shared-instruction duplicate execution pattern requiring human review, not automatic correction.

analysis.root_cause_title: Shared customer intent with repeated submission held before execution
analysis.root_cause_explanation: The two requests share the same business instruction and intent anchor, and the later request was received 5 seconds after the first. The first payment completed and posted once, while the second was held before execution and explicitly matched duplicate control to the earlier payment. This supports a confirmed duplicate request pattern rather than two independently authorized instructions. The evidence does not show the physical trigger, so the cause is described as repeated submission under shared intent rather than a literal double-click. Verified facts: the original request completed and posted once via journal JRN-D9269292EE384041, and the duplicate request remained held with no posting. The duplicate-control events indicate the system recognized the match to the earlier payment before execution.

facts.statement: The original payment completed and posted once through journal JRN-D9269292EE384041.
The duplicate payment was held before execution and has no posted journal in this snapshot.
Both requests reference the same business instruction identifier.
The later request was received 5 seconds after the earlier request.
Duplicate control matched the later request to the earlier payment before execution and blocked posting.

hypotheses.statement: The repeated submission may reflect the customer resubmitting the same payment intent after the first submission, but the source does not identify the physical trigger or user action beyond USER_SUBMIT.

uncertainty: The exact user trigger is unknown; the data shows USER_SUBMIT but not whether this was a retry, refresh, or other action.
OutcomeAvailability is NOT_RECORDED for both requests, so no additional downstream outcome details are available beyond the held status.
The detector configuration and thresholds are not provided, so no rule-level decision trace can be inferred beyond the recorded duplicate-control events.
analysis.recommendation_reason: This is a confirmed shared-intent duplicate request where one payment posted and the repeat was held before execution. A human closure review is appropriate, with no automatic financial correction.
